# Vendored noble-secp256k1 snapshot

Upstream: [paulmillr/noble-secp256k1](https://github.com/paulmillr/noble-secp256k1).
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paulmillr/noble-secp256k1/main/index.ts
Retrieved: 9 October 2026. The retrieval source reported its snapshot crawled six days earlier.

`index.ts` is the complete retrieved upstream source, with its MIT copyright header. No cryptographic algorithm is authored or modified by Goalstr. `compiled/index.js` and `compiled/index.d.ts` are generated by the project's pinned TypeScript compiler; source and output SHA-256 hashes are recorded in `PROVENANCE.json`. This is a frozen source snapshot, **not a claim that we installed or verified a particular npm release/commit**. Upstream main may have changed since retrieval. Update deliberately, retain its license, regenerate the outputs, and rerun the official BIP-340 vectors.

Package-registry downloads were unavailable in the build environment. The dependency-free async Schnorr API uses standard Web Crypto hashing and is isolated behind `src/protocol/nips/01/events.ts`. The rest of the app and pure domain have no noble imports. The verifier uses `schnorr.verifyAsync`; signing is used only by `scripts/generate-fixtures.ts`, with deliberately public test identities. The application has no identity-key input/generation or publishing flow.

Recompile the exact source with Node 24.x:

```sh
npx tsc --ignoreConfig vendor/noble-secp256k1/index.ts --target ES2022 --module ESNext --lib ES2022,DOM --skipLibCheck --declaration --removeComments --outDir vendor/noble-secp256k1/compiled
```

Verify with `npm test`. The tests include all 19 official BIP-340 positive/negative vectors, including variable-length messages. The vector corpus is from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitcoin/bips/master/bip-0340/test-vectors.csv and is used only in tests. The verifier separately checks the NIP-01 serialized event hash; a valid Schnorr signature alone does not establish that the event's ID matches its fields.

The larger nostr-tools SDK remains the planned relay/signer dependency for later stages. Its current official repository metadata identifies the npm package as `nostr-tools` at `2.25.2`, despite the README's `@nostr/tools`/JSR examples. That metadata was reviewed, but package installation and relay/NIP-46 runtime APIs remain an integration spike before Stage 3/5. No fake SDK module or custom cryptography substitutes for that future integration.
